text:
Alex K: Heads-up — three OOMs on prod-runner-7 during the 50k-token long-context E2E suite this morning. Noticed KV cache jumped ~1.9GB in <10s before the crash. :eyes:
Maria T: Ack. Which model/variant and which kernel?
Alex K: gptx-16k (v2.1), cuda-cu11 kernels. Profiling shows a lot of small allocations in kvcache arena, high fragmentation.
Jin L: Do we have pprof/heap dumps from the runner?
Alex K: Uploaded a heap dump to /artifacts/1925004321/heap-prod-runner-7.pb. Quick summary from pprof:
```
kvcache.slab_alloc: 62%
kv_page_meta: 18%
loader.temp_buffers: 8%
other: 12%
```
Sam P: 62% slab_alloc is alarming. Could be many tiny writes causing internal fragmentation. Any recent change to reuse policy?
Alex K: Yes — last week we shipped reuse policy tweak: prefer fresh pages for near-full spans to reduce read amplification. Might be the regression.
Pat G: That tweak reduced read latency in regen tests, but we didn't have long-context VMs in canary. Looks like tradeoff backfired for long contexts.
Maria T: For immediate mitigation, can we flip reuse policy back via feature flag and roll a hotfix?
Jin L: We can, but need a faster fallback: implement a soft-evict sweep when free_pct < 15% to avoid abrupt OOMs. Also cap per-request kvcache growth to X MB.
Alex K: Agreed. Proposed hotfix:
- roll back reuse policy (flag off)
- add emergency soft-evict sweep triggered by metrics.kv_free_pct < 18%
- limit per-request kvcache delta to 48MB
- add an allocation path fallback: on kvcache alloc failure, drop to streaming-only path and return partial KV-backed output with header `x-kv-degraded: 1`
Sam P: Sounds reasonable. How long to patch and ship canary?
Jin L: I have the patch mostly ready for the soft-evict and per-request cap. Can cut a canary build in ~2h. Rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows.
Maria T: Add metric alerts: oom_count, kv_free_pct, kv_frag_ratio, per_request_kv_bytes. Create dashboards and a short-stop SLO: if oom_count > 0 in 30m for canary, rollback to previous image.
Pat G: Also recommend changing default page size for kvcache from 64k -> 32k for long-context users; lower page size reduces internal wastage for lots of small KV nodes. Ship as a config tweak behind a flag.
Alex K: Good call. We'll gate page-size change to dedicated/runners running long-context tests only.
ops-bot: deploy job started: canary/prod-runner-7 -> image: kvcache-hotfix-1925 (triggered by Jin L).
Sam P: For longer-term fixes: compaction sweep thread, smarter slab allocator (bin small buckets), and an allocator profiler we can run in prod safely. Add to roadmap.
Maria T: Suggest adding a degraded-mode contract: if KV allocation fails, we should: 1) emit `x-kv-degraded`, 2) attempt 2 retries with exponential backoff (500ms -> 1s), 3) if still failing, stream partial tokens and set a trace `kv_degraded=true`. That will keep clients alive.
Alex K: I'll draft the PR and include tests that simulate repeated small KV writes under long contexts. Also adding unit test for eviction sweep correctness.
Jin L: Once canary is up, I'll run the 50k-token E2E suite against canary runners to validate memory curve is stable.
Pat G: FYI, load-testing script to reproduce: `python tools/long_ctx_kv_repro.py --tokens 50000 --writes 120000 --concurrency 8` — saved under /tools/repro.
Alex K: Thanks — assigning tasks in Github and will link the PR here. Keep reactions here for status. :thumbsup:
